column3: With respect to the Colonial Pointe Mortgage Loan (2.3%), the property is subject to a Land Use Restriction Agreement (“LURA”) that imposes affordable housing-related use restrictions in connection with the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (“LIHTC”) program (Section 42 of the Internal Revenue Code). The property was included in the LIHTC program in December 2001. As part of the property’s benefiting from a $8,750,000 bond issue from the South Carolina State Housing Finance and Development Authority for property rehabilitation, 100% of the subject units are rent- and income-restricted to households at 60% of AMI levels. The current use restrictions expire in December 2031. In addition, compliance with the more stringent Section 42 affordable housing restrictions qualified the mortgaged property for a 100% real estate property tax exemption pursuant to SC Statute 12-37-220(B)(11)(e). The borrower was granted a real estate tax exemption in January 2025. The property tax exemption requires that 40% of units be set aside for residents that earn 60% of AMI or less, and 35% of units be set aside for residents that earn 80% of AMI or less. The remaining 25% of units can be rented at market rates. The loan underwriting was based on a 100% exemption from real property taxes. If the property tax exemption is not maintained during the loan term, the loan documents provide that the borrower and guarantors are obligated to pay-down the loan in an amount required to achieve the greater of (A) an 8.0% debt yield or (B) a 1.25x DSCR (IO) based on loan underwriting that includes fully-loaded real property taxes. Further, the loan documents provide that the borrower and guarantors have springing recourse liability for the amount of such pay-down if not timely made.
